skill.name: ghe-checkpoint
skill.description: Creates structured progress checkpoints for active GitHub Issue threads and matching GHE_REPORTS records. It captures tasks, changed files, commits, blockers, branch state, and next actions without moving workflow phases.
skill.summary: Records current work state to an active GitHub Issue without changing phases.
skill.author: Emasoft

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command hits are false positives from Markdown inline code and fences. The home-directory finding is confirmed because the skill allows writes to ~/.claude. Semantic review also found instruction-hierarchy override language that should be removed before publication.

remediation.suggestion: Remove absolute rules that say user instructions must always be followed. State that actions must comply with system, developer, and security policies.
Do not allow background agents to write to ~/.claude by default. Require explicit user approval and document exact files before any settings change.
Define what thread-manager and memory-sync agents may access before posting checkpoints or updating activeContext.md.

content.value_statement: Long development sessions can lose state across tools, agents, and handoffs. This skill records a structured checkpoint in the active GitHub Issue thread and GHE_REPORTS.
actual_capabilities: Checks for an active claimed issue before posting a checkpoint.
Collects completed tasks, pending tasks, files changed, commits, branch, blockers, and next action.
Chooses a dev, test, or review thread manager from the thread type.
Requires full report text in both the GitHub Issue thread and GHE_REPORTS.
Updates activeContext.md through the memory-sync agent when enabled.
Keeps the current workflow phase unchanged.
limitations: Requires an existing claimed issue with an in-progress label.
Depends on companion thread-manager and memory-sync agents.
Does not complete phases or move work to another workflow state.
May expose project details if checkpoint text contains sensitive information.

use_cases.title: Developer Session Handoff
use_cases.description: Capture completed work, open tasks, branch state, and next action before another agent or teammate continues.

use_cases.title: Test Run Progress Log
use_cases.description: Record blockers, files changed, and pending validation while a test issue stays in progress.

use_cases.title: Review Workflow Checkpoint
use_cases.description: Post a concise state snapshot for reviewers without closing the current review phase.

prompt_templates.title: Save Current Progress
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner checkpoint during an active issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ghe-checkpoint to record what I finished, what is still pending, current blockers, and the next action.

prompt_templates.title: Checkpoint Before Session End
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a checkpoint for the active GitHub Issue before this session ends. Include changed files, commits, branch, blockers, and next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Document a Blocker
prompt_templates.prompt: Post a checkpoint that focuses on the current blocker, evidence gathered, attempted fixes, affected files, and the decision needed.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Cross-Agent Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a detailed checkpoint for the active thread. Separate completed, in-progress, and pending work, then sync the memory context.

output_examples.input: Save a checkpoint before I stop work on the active development issue.
output: Checkpoint posted to the active GitHub Issue.
GHE_REPORTS received the same full report.
Memory context updated with next action.

output_examples.input: I found a blocker during test validation.
output: Progress snapshot recorded with blocker details.
Pending tests and affected files were listed.
The issue remains in progress for follow-up.

output_examples.input: Prepare handoff for a review thread.
output_examples.output: The checkpoint summarizes completed review work, unresolved comments, files touched, current branch, and the next reviewer action.

best_practices: Run the skill only after a GitHub Issue is claimed and labeled in progress.
Include concrete file names, commit hashes, blockers, and next actions in each checkpoint.
Review sensitive details before posting checkpoint text to a GitHub Issue.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill to close a phase or move work to the next phase.
Do not run it when no active issue thread is assigned to you.
Do not post secrets, private credentials, or unreleased business details in checkpoints.

faq.question: Does this skill change workflow phases?
faq.answer: No. It saves progress only. Use the transition skill when a phase must move forward.

faq.question: Does it require an active GitHub Issue?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill expects a claimed issue with an in-progress label before checkpointing.

faq.question: What information is captured?
faq.answer: It captures work log, tasks, files changed, commits, branch, blockers, and next action.

faq.question: Where does the checkpoint go?
faq.answer: The skill expects full checkpoint text in the GitHub Issue thread and GHE_REPORTS.

faq.question: Can memory sync be skipped?
faq.answer: Yes. Local settings can disable SERENA memory sync when configured that way.

faq.question: Is this safe for sensitive projects?
faq.answer: Use caution. Review checkpoint content before posting because issue comments can expose project details.
